relationship: Editing assembly source connects symbolic instructions to the assembler passes, CPU phases and program input/output.

learnerLoop.action: Choose or edit a program, then step or run it.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The source is assembled and the processor state advances through its instruction phases.
learnerLoop.evidence: The assembly summary, translation table, registers, phases and console expose the result.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Fix the source or predict the next instruction effect.

invariants: Source, translated instructions and execution evidence remain consistent.
Stepping preserves the visible instruction-by-instruction trace.
safeAdaptations: Change example programs, input values, pacing or explanatory language while retaining the assembler-to-CPU trace.
nonGoals: Teaching an unspecified real-world assembly dialect beyond the lab's model.

task.description: Program goal and six supplied assembly examples.
task.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

source.description: Editable source with two-pass label resolution and assembly diagnostics.
source.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

model.description: CPU beside system buses and RAM; highlighted transfers follow micro-operations.
model.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

evidence.description: ASCII output, assembly summary and execution position.
evidence.visibility: Present in the corresponding simulation or construction state.

source.domain: Supported instructions, labels and stored data; invalid source blocks execution.
source.output: Assembler diagnostics, resolved addresses and RAM.

cpu.description: Register and memory state after each micro-operation.
cpu.domain: The lab CPU model and assembled memory.
cpu.source: Step/Run from the selected entry address.
cpu.output: Register values, highlighted transfers, memory changes and output.

modes.program: Six supplied examples plus editable source.
modes.execution: Single micro-operation or timed run at three speeds.
modes.support: No Working, exam toggle or scored completion.

dependencies: Editing source reassembles and resets execution.
Run and Step consume the same micro-operation queue; IN consumes the ASCII input buffer.
implementation.completion: END halts execution; invalid source and runtime errors stop execution without a success score.
limitations: Cambridge-style teaching dialect; not a machine-code emulator.
RAM and source tables retain useful scrolling; the CPU diagram itself fits its container.
